successCriteria.description: Create `src/modules/leave/leave-policy.model.ts` exporting a `LeavePolicy` interface with all specified fields: id (string), policyName (string), leaveType (LeaveType enum imported from `src/shared/types/index.ts`), entitlementDays (number), accrualRate (number), maxAccumulation (number), minimumNoticeDays (number), requiresManagerApproval (boolean), isActive (boolean), allowsNegativeBalance (boolean), maxConsecutiveDays (number), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date).

Create `src/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.ts` exporting an `ILeavePolicyRepository` interface with methods: `findById(id: string): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>`, `findAll(): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>`, `findByLeaveType(leaveType: LeaveType): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>`, `create(policy: Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeavePolicy>`, `update(id: string, policy: Partial<LeavePolicy>): Promise<LeavePolicy>`, `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>`.

Implement `LeavePolicyRepository` class extending `BaseRepository<LeavePolicy>` (from `src/shared/base-repository.ts`) and implementing `ILeavePolicyRepository`. Constructor accepts optional `Pool` override. All methods delegate to `this.pool.query` via the protected `query` method. `findById` is the concrete implementation of the abstract method from `BaseRepository`.

Create `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave-policy.repository.test.ts` with Jest unit tests that mock the pg Pool and verify all six repository methods (findById, findAll, findByLeaveType, create, update, softDelete) behave correctly — including success paths and edge cases like findById returning null for missing records.

constraints: Must import `LeaveType` from `src/shared/types/index.ts` (Phase 1 artifact) — do not redefine or duplicate the enum.

`LeavePolicyRepository` must extend `BaseRepository<LeavePolicy>` from `src/shared/base-repository.ts` (Phase 2 artifact) and implement the abstract `findById(id: string): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>` method.
All database access must go through the repository's protected `query` method inherited from `BaseRepository` — no direct `pool.query` calls (GP-001).
Strict TypeScript: no `any` types; use `unknown` with type guards where needed (HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`).
Constructor must accept an optional `Pool` override (matching the `BaseRepository` pattern) to support testability with mocked pools.
outOfScope: No service layer, controller, or routes for leave policy — those belong to later phases (Phase 6–8).
No database migrations or table creation — this phase defines only the TypeScript model interface and repository class.
No audit logging (GP-002) or RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — those are service-layer and route-layer concerns respectively, not repository-layer.
No input validation beyond TypeScript type-checking — GP-003 validation at API boundaries is a controller concern (Phase 7).

ambiguities.description: The `softDelete` method semantics are not explicitly specified — should it set `isActive = false`, set a `deletedAt` timestamp, or both? The architecture defines the lifecycle as ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE → ARCHIVED, suggesting `isActive = false` is the intended behavior.
options: Set isActive = false and record deletedAt timestamp
Set isActive = false and set status to ARCHIVED

ambiguities.description: The `update` method accepts `Partial<LeavePolicy>` — should `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` be excluded from the partial update payload? The intent does not specify which fields are immutable.
options: Exclude id, createdAt, updatedAt from the partial type
Only allow updating a specific subset of mutable fields
